title: Follow the Path in Nested Data
content:
What problem does this solve?
Real programs combine the structures you already know. A list can contain dictionaries, and a dictionary can contain a list. Do not try to read a long nested expression all at once. Take one step, identify what value and type you reached, then take the next step.

One step at a time
  party[0]
selects one dictionary from a list. Then
  party[0]["health"]
reads one field from that dictionary.

Dictionary to list
  record["tags"]
produces a list. Adding [1] then selects its second item.

Update the path you mean
A nested assignment changes the inner value reached by the full path. Start from the outside structure and verify each step before writing the update.

Vocabulary after the behavior
Nested data means one collection stored inside another. A path is the sequence of indexes/keys used to reach an inner value.
concepts: Trace nested access from left to right one step at a time
A list index can lead to a dictionary
A dictionary key can lead to a list
The final part of a nested path identifies the inner value being read or changed
Name an intermediate value when a long path is hard to reason about

examples.title: List of dictionaries
examples.explanation: people[0] gives one dictionary; ["name"] then reads a field from it.

examples.title: Dictionary containing a list
examples.explanation: record["tags"] is a list; [1] chooses its second item.

examples.title: Update an inner value
examples.explanation: The complete path ends at the score inside the first record.

common_mistakes: Looking for an inner key on the outer structure
Forgetting to index a list before asking for a key inside one record
Memorizing a long path instead of checking each intermediate value
Updating a separate temporary collection instead of the collection stored inside the model
Introducing a new iteration tool when existing range/indexing is enough

exercises.title: One step, then another
hints: First evaluate people[1].
That produces the second dictionary, {"name": "Bo"}.
Then ["name"] reads Bo.

exercises.title: Read the inner list
exercises.prompt: Replace the placeholder index so the program prints `urgent`.
hints: First evaluate record["tags"] and identify the resulting list.
urgent is the second item, and list indexes begin at 0.
Use index 1: `record["tags"][1]`.

exercises.title: Name the intermediate value
exercises.prompt:
After this code runs, what kind of value is stored in `member`?

party = [{"name": "Mira", "health": 8}]
member = party[0]
hints: Evaluate only party[0].
The outer value is a list whose first item is a record with keys name and health.
member is a dictionary.
exercises.success_message: Correct. Naming the intermediate dictionary makes the next path step easier to reason about.

exercises.title: Update the inner value
exercises.prompt: Increase the first player's score by 2 using the nested path. Then print the new score.
exercises.starter_code:
players = [{"name": "A", "score": 3}, {"name": "B", "score": 5}]

# Update the first score by 2.
hints: Start by identifying the first record: players[0].
Use the same nested path on both sides of the assignment, adding 2 on the right.
Assign `players[0]["score"] = players[0]["score"] + 2`, then print that path.

exercises.title: Trace a longer path
hints: Move left to right and identify the type after every step.
record["groups"] is a list; [0] is a dictionary; ["items"] is another list.
Index 1 of ["a", "b"] is b.

exercises.title: Look inside the party
exercises.prompt: The name is inside the first member dictionary, not directly inside dispatch. Repair the access path so it prints Mira.
hints: Start with a key that actually exists on dispatch.
dispatch["party"] gives a list, so choose its first member before asking for name.
Use `dispatch["party"][0]["name"]`.

exercises.title: Total party health
exercises.prompt: Write `total_party_health(party)` that loops over a list of member dictionaries and returns the sum of every `member["health"]`. It must return 0 for an empty party.
hints: Start a running total at 0 and visit every member dictionary.
On each pass add member["health"] to the running total.
Return total after the loop, so an empty party naturally returns 0.

exercises.title: Numbered Roster
exercises.prompt: Write `numbered_roster(party)` using `range(len(party))` and indexing. Return a list of lines exactly like `1. Mira — 8 HP`. Visit every nested member record; do not print inside the function.
hints: Build a result list and generate valid party indexes with range(len(party)).
For each index, first store `member = party[index]`, then read that member dictionary.
Append the formatted 1-based line to lines and return lines after the loop.
exercises.success_message: The roster combines old indexing/range skills with nested records and a structured returned result.
